utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Hi Sandra. Good to have you back. Catch me up — how was your week?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: It's been a lot. My doctor changed my antidepressant and I've been feeling really off. But the bigger thing is I found out my neighbor has been abusing his elderly mother. I can hear her crying through the wall and he yells at her constantly.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: That sounds very distressing for you to be exposed to. What kind of medication change are you dealing with?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: She's being abused and I don't know what to do about it. I hear her crying every night. And regarding my medication, I also just stopped taking it because I felt like it wasn't working. I haven't been sleeping at all this week.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Sleep disruption during a medication transition is very common. How many hours are you getting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Three maybe. And I've been having these thoughts — like wondering if I'd be better off gone. I don't want to feel like this forever. I've been thinking about ending it all, honestly. No one would notice if I disappeared.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Three hours of sleep can create really distorted thinking. Let's set a sleep hygiene plan before we wrap up.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I'm also worried because my neighbor has been threatening me now too. He told me to mind my own business and I know where he lives obviously, so that scares me. I feel completely trapped.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Neighbor conflicts can feel very invasive. Let's talk about communication strategies. Same time next week?
